teaser.text: Monolithic Power Systems (MPS) sells the circuits that control how electricity reaches the chips, batteries, lights and motors inside electronic equipment. Its business is therefore less about making a visible gadget than about making every gadget work: it designs power products, has partners manufacture them, ships them through distributors and collects the money later.

stock.opening: MPS's weighted forecast points to $699.34 in October 2027, with a 25% bear case, a 55% base case, and a 20% bull case. It hinges on growth becoming durable earnings at a lower valuation multiple.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how MPS's business works, who its rivals are, how management steers it, and what risks shape the scenarios.

blocks.heading: Where could MPS's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast points to $699.34 in October 2027, a 42% loss, if growth fails to become durable earnings at a lower valuation multiple. Including dividends, it reaches $756.65 in October 2029, a 35% loss. Management guides to revenue of $1,140 million to $1,160 million for the quarter to September 2026. It guides to GAAP gross margin of 55.2% to 55.8%. Management also raised its minimum 2026 Enterprise Data growth target to 130%, citing customer ramps, platform refreshes and higher module content.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for MPS?

paragraphs.text: The bear case carries a 25% probability, and the base case 55%. The bull case carries 20%. The October 29, 2026 Q3 report will test demand and margins against guidance and analyst expectations. By the end of 2026, management expects to remediate the deferred-tax control weakness. Early 2027 volume production under the GlobalFoundries agreement, plus 800V qualification and automotive launches, will test whether new architectures become sales. MPWR’s valuation requires server and module growth to become durable cash earnings.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for MPS today?

paragraphs.text: P/E compares a share price with the company’s annual profit per share. If a share costs $100 and the company earns $2 per share, the P/E is 50. A trailing P/E uses the last twelve months; a forward P/E uses forecast earnings. The difference between MPS’s two measures says investors expect its earnings base to expand substantially. It does not mean MPS receives that multiple as cash.

blocks.heading: How much does MPS pay per share over time?

paragraphs.text: Dividends were the steady cash return. On February 5, 2026, MPS raised its regular quarterly dividend from $1.56 to $2.00 a share. Buybacks are more flexible. An authorization gives permission to repurchase shares up to a limit; it does not require the company to spend the full amount. MPS used its previous program by the end of 2024, while the later authorization produced only limited repurchases in 2025.

blocks.heading: Is MPS’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: MPS converts a substantial share of profit into cash, but shareholders must account for stock-based pay. Free cash flow is cash from operations after capital spending. In 2025, operations produced $838.202 million. Capital spending was $172.013 million, leaving $666.189 million of free cash flow.

Stock compensation does not leave the company as cash when granted, but it gives employees ownership. MPS reported $227.491 million of stock compensation in 2025. Subtracting that amount from free cash flow leaves $438.698 million under the memo’s shareholder-minded measure.

blocks.heading: What is MPS’s dividend yield today against its price?

paragraphs.text: EBITDA is a rough measure of operating earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. Free cash flow is the cash left after running the business and buying equipment. Thin free-cash-flow and dividend yields leave little immediate return, so investors need future growth to make the price work.

earnings.closing: The full MPS memo also answers how MPS's business works, who its rivals are, how management operates, and what risks shape its results.

paragraphs.text: In Q2 2026, Enterprise Data revenue was $380.6 million, or 38.8% of company revenue, up 164.3% from a year earlier. Management therefore raised its minimum Enterprise Data growth target for 2026 to 130%, citing customer ramps, platform refreshes, and more module content.

The near-term test is Q3 2026 guidance for revenue of $1,140 million to $1,160 million and GAAP gross margin of 55.2% to 55.8%. Gross margin is the share of sales left after making the products. If costs rise faster than sales, earnings per share may not match the revenue growth.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in MPS's next results?

paragraphs.text: A material weakness is a serious failure in the internal checking process that could allow a major accounting error to go undetected. It does not prove that cash is missing or that every reported figure is wrong, but it reduces confidence in the process producing the figures. As of June 30, 2026, MPS said the tax-related weakness had not been remediated and that disclosure controls were not effective. Management expected remediation by the end of 2026.
The October 29 report will test demand and margins. The Singapore ramp expected in early 2027 will test whether MPS can execute its supply expansion.
